result.summary: Optimizes the script interpreter function CastToBool by scanning stack elements in 64-bit (8-byte) chunks instead of byte by byte. CastToBool determines boolean truthiness by inspecting byte vectors for any non-zero bytes (accounting for negative zero representations). This reduces the number of loop iterations required when validating large stack elements.
result.problem: CastToBool currently inspects byte arrays one byte at a time. For long stack elements (up to the standard 520-byte limit) that contain trailing non-zero bytes or repeated zeros, evaluating truthiness for opcodes like OP_IFDUP and OP_VERIFY causes unnecessary CPU overhead in script verification.
evidence: Author benchmark on a synthetic worst-case script using a 520-byte element (519 zero bytes followed by 0x01) with repeated IFDUP VERIFY demonstrates a 3.1x speedup in VerifyIfDupVerifyFullLast from ~922ms to ~295ms (PR description and commit 2d5f67c986).
result.scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the prompt metadata, but git stats indicate a 12-line change (+10/-2 in 1 file), likely in src/script/script.cpp or src/script/interpreter.cpp.
result.card: Optimizes the script interpreter's CastToBool function by inspecting stack elements in 64-bit chunks instead of byte-by-byte. In current nodes, truthiness checks on large byte vectors incur linear per-byte overhead, allowing adversarial scripts with large near-zero byte arrays to waste CPU during transaction verification. The author measures a 3.1x speedup (922ms to 295ms) on a synthetic 520-byte repeated OP_IFDUP/OP_VERIFY benchmark.
uncertainties: Exact loop implementation, word-alignment handling, and tail-byte logic cannot be confirmed without the patch diff.

risk.why: CastToBool directly dictates script condition evaluation, so any discrepancy or memory safety bug in chunked scanning could cause a consensus split.
